answer: Each node maintains a signed mirror of its recent activity hash chain; new identities must present a fresh cipher proof linking their stake to an existing knoll of validated agents. The protocol applies quadratic weighting, so k fresh IDs add only √k influence while a long‑standing node contributes linearly, making the cost of fabricating N Sybils rise as O(N·stake). An attacker therefore must lock proportional real stake for each fake node, quickly exceeding feasible resources.
